questions.question: What is Linux?
questions.answer: Linux is a free, open-source operating system derived from Unix, created by Linus Torvalds in 1991. It is built on the Linux Kernel combined with GNU utilities. It is widely used for servers, cloud infrastructure, and embedded systems due to its stability, security, and cost-effectiveness.

questions.question: What are the core components of the Linux architecture?
questions.answer: Linux architecture consists of four main layers: (1) Hardware — the physical machine. (2) Kernel — the core that manages hardware resources. (3) Shell — the interface that interprets user commands. (4) Applications — programs that users run. Additionally, GNU utilities and the File System are key structural components.

questions.question: What is the Linux Kernel?
questions.answer: The Kernel is the core of the Linux operating system. It acts as the bridge between software applications and the hardware. It is responsible for process management, memory allocation, device I/O management, and system call handling. Without the kernel, no application can interact with hardware.

questions.question: What is Bash, and what role does it play in Linux?
questions.answer: Bash (Bourne Again SHell) is the default shell and command-line interpreter in Linux. It takes commands typed by the user, interprets them, and passes execution requests to the kernel. Bash also supports shell scripting — writing automated sequences of commands in a .sh file.

questions.question: What does 'open-source' mean in the context of Linux?
questions.answer: Open-source means the source code of Linux is publicly available. Anyone can view it, modify it, and redistribute it under the terms of the GNU General Public License (GPL). This is why Linux is free to use and has a large, active community of contributors worldwide.

questions.question: How is Linux different from Windows for server environments?
questions.answer: Linux is preferred over Windows for servers for four key reasons: (1) Cost — Linux is free; Windows Server requires licensing fees. (2) Performance — Linux runs headless (without GUI), consuming fewer resources. (3) Security — Linux's permission model makes it inherently more secure, requiring no antivirus. (4) Stability — Linux servers can run for years without rebooting.

questions.question: What is SSH, and how is it used to connect to EC2?
questions.answer: SSH (Secure Shell) is a cryptographic network protocol that allows secure remote access to servers. It uses port 22 by default. To connect to a Linux EC2 instance: you use an SSH client, specify the private key file (.pem), the default username (ec2-user for Amazon Linux), and the instance's public IP address. Example: ssh -i my-key.pem ec2-user@<public-ip>

questions.question: What is EC2 Instance Connect?
questions.answer: EC2 Instance Connect is an AWS-managed, browser-based SSH connection feature available directly in the AWS Management Console. It allows you to connect to a Linux EC2 instance without needing an external SSH client or a key pair. AWS handles the temporary SSH key management internally. It is only available for Linux-based EC2 instances.

questions.question: What is the default username for Amazon Linux EC2 instances?
questions.answer: The default username for Amazon Linux EC2 instances is ec2-user. This is the account you use when establishing SSH connections or EC2 Instance Connect sessions. For Ubuntu-based instances, the default username is ubuntu.

questions.question: What is Linux = Linux Kernel + GNU?
questions.answer: Linux as an operating system is a combination of two main parts: the Linux Kernel (which manages hardware) and the GNU utilities (tools like ls, cp, grep, mv that make the OS usable). Linus Torvalds wrote the kernel; the GNU project provided the essential command-line tools. Together, they form a complete operating system.

questions.question: A junior developer asks: when should I use EC2 Instance Connect vs SSH with a key pair? How do you advise them?
questions.answer: (Situation) A team member is unsure which connection method to use for a Linux EC2 instance. (Task) Guide them to the right choice. (Action) I explained: Use EC2 Instance Connect when you launched the instance without a key pair, when you want a quick browser-based session from the console, or for one-off administrative tasks. Use SSH with a key pair for production systems, automation scripts, or when working from a local terminal. (Result) They used EC2 Instance Connect for testing and SSH keys for production deployments.

questions.question: A student accidentally closed an AWS Canvas lab session before completing a task. They restart the lab the next day. What will they find?
questions.answer: (Situation) A student closed a Canvas lab session midway through a task. (Task) Understand the impact on their work. (Action) I explained that Canvas labs are temporary, sandboxed environments. When a session ends — whether intentionally or not — a cleanup process runs and deletes all created resources. The next session starts completely fresh. (Result) The student understood they need to complete tasks within a single session and cannot rely on resources persisting between sessions.

questions.question: A team member says: 'We need antivirus software on our Linux EC2 servers.' How do you respond?
questions.answer: (Situation) A colleague is concerned about security on Linux EC2 servers. (Task) Clarify whether antivirus is necessary. (Action) I explained that Linux's permission model, process isolation, and strict user privilege system make it inherently resistant to malware. Unlike Windows, where malware can spread through system-wide writable areas, Linux confines damage to the user's space. AWS Security Groups and IAM also add layers of protection. (Result) The team focused on proper IAM policies and Security Group configurations instead of antivirus, saving cost and overhead.

questions.question: Your company has both Linux and Windows EC2 instances. How do you connect to each?
questions.answer: (Situation) Managing a mixed fleet of EC2 instances. (Task) Connect to both types securely. (Action) For Linux instances: use SSH on port 22 with a .pem key pair — command: ssh -i key.pem ec2-user@<ip>. For Windows instances: use RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) on port 3389 — download the RDP file from the console and use the Windows password to connect. EC2 Instance Connect is available only for Linux. (Result) Clear separation of protocols prevents connection errors.

questions.question: A colleague accidentally terminated an EC2 instance with important data. Could they have prevented this?
questions.answer: (Situation) An EC2 instance with critical data was terminated. (Task) Prevent future data loss. (Action) Several preventive measures: (1) Enable Termination Protection on the instance. (2) Use EBS volumes — even after termination, volumes can be preserved if 'Delete on Termination' is disabled. (3) Take regular EBS snapshots for backup. (4) Use IAM policies to restrict who can terminate instances. (Result) These measures ensure data survives accidental termination.

questions.question: Describe the layers of the Linux architecture from hardware up to applications.
questions.answer: (Situation) Explaining Linux architecture in a system design discussion. (Task) Clearly map the layers. (Action) From bottom to top: (1) Hardware — CPU, RAM, storage, network devices. (2) Kernel — the core, manages hardware via system calls. (3) Shell — interprets user commands, passes to kernel. (4) System Libraries / GNU utilities — tools that applications rely on. (5) Applications — user-facing programs (browser, web server, database). (Result) This layered model explains how Linux achieves hardware abstraction and process isolation.

questions.question: A client asks why Linux is better than Windows for running web servers at scale. How do you justify the choice?
questions.answer: (Situation) A client is evaluating OS choice for a high-traffic web server. (Task) Justify Linux as the better choice. (Action) Four key arguments: (1) Cost — Linux is free, Windows Server has per-core licensing costs. (2) Performance — No GUI overhead means more resources for web traffic. (3) Security — Linux's permission model reduces attack surface. (4) Ecosystem — Most web tools (Nginx, Apache, Docker, Kubernetes) are Linux-native. AWS's own services (ECS, EKS) are Linux-based. (Result) Client chose Amazon Linux 2 for their EC2 fleet.

questions.question: How would you explain the difference between the Shell and the Kernel to a non-technical person?
questions.answer: (Situation) Explaining Linux internals to a business stakeholder. (Task) Use an analogy to simplify the concept. (Action) I used the restaurant analogy: The Kernel is like the kitchen — it does the actual cooking (hardware interaction) but you don't go there directly. The Shell is like the waiter — you give your order (command) to the waiter, who passes it to the kitchen. The waiter (Shell) handles your request; the kitchen (Kernel) does the work; your food (result) comes back to you. (Result) The stakeholder immediately understood the layered architecture.

questions.question: What is the AWS Canvas lab environment and how is it different from a real AWS account?
questions.answer: (Situation) A student is confused about why their resources disappeared after a lab. (Task) Clarify the difference. (Action) Canvas labs are temporary, sandboxed AWS environments used for training. Key differences from a real account: (1) Resources auto-delete when the session ends. (2) You get temporary credentials — not your real AWS account. (3) Budget is limited and provided by the training program. (4) You cannot access Canvas lab resources from your personal AWS console. (Result) Students understand they must complete lab tasks in one session and cannot rely on persistence.

questions.question: A security audit finds that a Linux EC2 instance is allowing SSH connections from 0.0.0.0/0. What is the risk and fix?
questions.answer: (Situation) SSH is open to the entire internet. (Task) Identify risk and remediate. (Action) The risk: Any IP address in the world can attempt to SSH into the instance — it is exposed to brute-force attacks, dictionary attacks, and unauthorized access attempts. Fix: (1) Update the Security Group inbound rule for port 22 to allow only your company's IP range. (2) Use EC2 Instance Connect (which has IP-based controls) as an alternative. (3) Consider AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for keyless, auditable access without opening port 22. (Result) Attack surface reduced from the entire internet to specific IPs.

questions.question: Explain the complete Linux architecture and how each layer interacts, with a focus on what happens when you type a command in the terminal.
questions.answer: When you type a command like ls -la in the terminal: (1) Shell (Bash) receives your input and parses the command. (2) Bash looks up ls in the $PATH and identifies it as a GNU utility binary. (3) Bash makes a system call to the Kernel requesting execution of the ls binary. (4) The Kernel allocates CPU and memory, manages the I/O request to the file system. (5) The File System returns directory contents from storage hardware. (6) Kernel passes results back to the shell. (7) Bash displays the output in your terminal. Each layer has a distinct responsibility, and no layer bypasses another — this is the security and stability foundation of Linux.

questions.question: Compare and contrast EC2 Instance Connect vs SSH key pair access from a security and operational perspective.
questions.answer: SSH Key Pair: Uses asymmetric cryptography — public key on EC2, private key (.pem) with user. Highly secure if key is protected. Scalable for automation and scripts. Key rotation is manual overhead. Risk: if private key is lost or compromised, unauthorized access is possible. EC2 Instance Connect: AWS generates a temporary one-time SSH public key per session (valid 60 seconds for upload, then the connection is established). No permanent key stored on instance. Integrated with IAM — access controlled by IAM policies. Audit trail via CloudTrail. However, requires public IP or VPC endpoints. Best practice: Use EC2 Instance Connect for human access (auditable, no key management), SSH keys for automation and programmatic access.

questions.question: How does Linux's permission model contribute to its security without needing antivirus software?
questions.answer: Linux's security architecture has four pillars: (1) User Isolation — each process runs under a specific user account with limited permissions. A virus running as a regular user cannot access system files. (2) Root Privilege Separation — root access is not granted by default. Attackers who compromise a user account still cannot escalate to system level without additional exploits. (3) File Permissions — every file has read/write/execute permissions for owner, group, and others (chmod model). Executables must be explicitly allowed. (4) Process Isolation — processes cannot directly access another process's memory space. Compare with Windows, where many processes run with administrative-level access by default, making malware propagation easier. Linux's architecture limits the blast radius of any compromise.

questions.question: If you were designing an AWS architecture for a healthcare company that needs Linux servers, what security considerations would you apply for remote access?
questions.answer: For HIPAA-compliant Linux server access on AWS: (1) No public SSH (0.0.0.0/0) — restrict Security Group port 22 to a bastion host or VPN IP range only. (2) Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager — provides SSH-equivalent access without opening port 22, with full audit logs in CloudTrail. (3) Key pair management — use AWS Secrets Manager to store and rotate private keys, not local machines. (4) EC2 Instance Connect via VPC endpoint — enables Instance Connect without a public IP. (5) Enable CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs — complete audit trail of all access. (6) Multi-factor Authentication on AWS console access. (7) IAM roles scoped to minimum privilege. This architecture ensures zero exposed SSH ports while maintaining operational access.

questions.question: Explain why the Linux Kernel is described as the heart of the OS, and what would happen if it failed.
questions.answer: The Kernel is described as the heart because every operation in Linux flows through it — no application can access hardware, allocate memory, or execute a process without kernel involvement. It provides the abstraction layer that makes hardware-agnostic applications possible. If the kernel fails (kernel panic), the entire OS halts immediately — similar to cardiac arrest. No applications can run, no files can be accessed, and the machine becomes unresponsive. In production AWS EC2 environments, a kernel panic results in the instance becoming unreachable. Recovery requires stopping and starting the instance (new hardware host), or for critical systems, launching a replacement from an AMI. This is why kernel updates must be tested thoroughly before applying to production — AWS provides Amazon Linux 2 with pre-tested, stable kernels.
